title: Grade 6 French — Tue, Jun 17
description: La nourriture — Day 2 of 5: Partitive articles
subject: french

questions.question: Which partitive article is used with a masculine noun beginning with a consonant?
questions.explanation: 'Du' is the partitive article for masculine nouns beginning with a consonant (du = de + le). Example: du pain (some bread).

questions.question: Choose the correct partitive article: 'Je mange ___ soupe.'
questions.explanation: La soupe is feminine, so we use 'de la'. Je mange de la soupe = I eat some soup.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the correct partitive article?
questions.explanation: Le lait (milk) is masculine, so we use 'du' (de + le). Je bois du lait = I drink some milk.

questions.question: What partitive article is used before a noun starting with a vowel?
questions.explanation: De l' is used before any noun (masculine or feminine) that starts with a vowel or silent h. Example: de l'eau (some water), de l'huile (some oil).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'Nous mangeons ___ légumes.' (légumes is plural)
questions.explanation: For plural nouns we use 'des'. Nous mangeons des légumes = We eat some vegetables.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence: 'I eat some rice.'
questions.explanation: Le riz (rice) is masculine, so we use 'du'. Je mange du riz = I eat some rice.

questions.question: Which partitive article completes the sentence: 'Elle boit ___ eau.'?
questions.explanation: L'eau (water) starts with a vowel, so we use 'de l''. Elle boit de l'eau = She drinks some water.

questions.question: What does 'beaucoup de' mean in quantity expressions?
questions.explanation: Beaucoup de means 'a lot of / much'. After quantity expressions like beaucoup de, un peu de, the partitive article is dropped.

questions.question: Which is correct: 'I drink a lot of water'?
questions.explanation: After 'beaucoup de', we use de/d' without any article. Beaucoup d'eau = a lot of water (d' before vowel).

questions.question: Fill in: 'Tu manges ___ fromage.' (fromage = masculine)
questions.explanation: Le fromage (cheese) is masculine, so we use 'du'. Tu manges du fromage = You eat some cheese.

questions.question: Which sentence means 'I eat some apples'?
questions.explanation: Pommes (apples) is plural, so we use 'des'. Je mange des pommes = I eat some apples.

questions.question: In negative sentences, partitive articles change to:
options: du / de la / de l' / des
questions.explanation: In negative sentences, all partitive articles (du, de la, de l', des) are replaced by 'de' (or 'd'' before a vowel). Example: Je ne mange pas de viande.

questions.question: Choose the correct negative sentence: 'I don't eat meat.'
options: Je ne mange pas du viande.
Je ne mange pas de viande.
Je ne mange pas la viande.
Je ne mange pas des viandes.
questions.explanation: In negatives, du/de la/des all become 'de'. Je ne mange pas de viande = I don't eat (any) meat.

questions.question: What does 'un peu de' mean?
questions.explanation: Un peu de means 'a little of'. Like beaucoup de, it is a quantity expression followed directly by the noun (no partitive article).

questions.question: Which is correct: 'She eats some pasta'?
questions.explanation: Les pâtes (pasta) is plural, so we use 'des'. Elle mange des pâtes = She eats some pasta.
